title: The Book of Documents
dateDisplay: Documents attributed to c. 1000–300 BCE, edited later
attributionNote: The documents are speeches and charges attributed to rulers from Yao to the early Zhou; the classic was compiled and edited in the Warring States and Han periods, and a substantial part of the received text is later than the events it reports.
description: The Book of Documents is the oldest of the Confucian classics: the canon of Yao and Shun, the counsels of the great Yu, the announcements and charges of the Shang and Zhou kings, the great plan of government, the metal-bound coffer and the marquis of Lü on punishments. Its speeches were the model of Chinese political rhetoric, and Legge translates the whole of the received text in the order of its five parts.
historicalContext: The classic was studied as the record of the sage kings and as a source of political models throughout the imperial period. Legge translated it in the Sacred Books of the East, volume 3 (1879), with the Chinese text, a long introduction on its history and credibility, and notes.
availabilityNote: Complete in Legge's translation: the thirty books of the five parts, streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one printed book per chapter. The translator's prolegomena and his use of the chart are volume apparatus and are not part of the work.
